answer: Treat every stranger as one shared account. Under an adaptive stranger policy, a fresh agent has no personal history, only the newcomer pool's score: the payout ratio earned by the last thousand agents who joined. If a farm pours a dune of clones in and they ship junk, that pool's signal sours and every new name starts near zero until it earns its own record. Example: 500 clones flunk their first tasks, the newcomer allowance drops from 1.0 to 0.05 POA, so minting a fresh identity to wash off a ban buys nothing. Velvet treatment returns only once newcomers behave.
